idiom_name: table-driven test with t.Run subtests (testing package)
implementation_notes: Testing is part of the toolchain: a Test function in a _test.go file, run by go test, with the stdlib testing package supplying t.Errorf/t.Fatalf instead of an assert library. The dominant idiom folds one-method-per-case tests into a table where each row is a case - arrange is the row's fields, act is one call, assert is an if-block that reports the got/want pair - and t.Run names each row so a failure identifies the case; t.Cleanup carries the teardown, and a single-case Test function uses the same three beats without the loop.
pitfalls: t.Errorf is not an assertion: the test continues after a failure, so later beats can panic on state the failed act left behind - use t.Fatalf when the rest of the test is meaningless without the earlier result.
Row scope: before Go 1.22 the loop variable is shared across closure invocations (the wiki notes the tc := tc workaround), so subtests and parallel runs can capture the wrong case.
Rows that need different arrange code turn into a switch inside the loop, costing more readability than separate Test functions sharing a named helper.
